clue.text: Love probing science with celebrity left-winger

indicators.note: something probing pushes its way into something else, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: SCI is the standard abbreviation for science
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A famous scientist with radical politics gets involved in research about love.
explanation.walkthrough: The love symbol goes inside the abbreviation for science, then the celebrity tier follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialist is a political figure of the left, so a left-winger in the political sense.

clue.text: Small, vain creep?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
idle can mean futile or pointless, as in idle threats

explanation.surface: A short, conceited person who is a toady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' reads as a noun for a sycophant, but it is the verb for moving stealthily.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move furtively or edge along sideways, a way of creeping.

clue.text: Promise to limit one rent's rising in support of local area?

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in or bound, so the promise wraps around what follows

parts.note: to commit is to pledge or promise
unity is oneness

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip; with the 's it is read as rips, then read upwards

explanation.surface: A pledge to cap rent rises would help the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like housing cost but means a tear. 'Rising' turns the rips upwards in this down clue, and unity plus that sits inside the promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Community spirit is the shared feeling of belonging and mutual help among neighbours.

clue.text: A blemish outside prison up in Indian city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece placed outside another surrounds it

parts.note: to mar is to spoil, here used as a blemish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means written bottom to top, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A stain on a jail in a city of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The slang jail goes upward in this down clue, then sits inside MAR, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in Punjab, northern India, home of the Golden Temple.

clue.text: Close situation I encountered in international store in America? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the store's name is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: INT is the abbreviation for international
taken as written
Macy's is a New York department store chain, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A cosy moment I came across in a big American shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given out of answer order: I is placed after the international abbreviation. Macy's is a large US department store.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimacy is the state of being close to someone, a situation of closeness.

clue.text: Crowd beginning to reappear, enthralled by daring beachwear

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a thong is a skimpy swimsuit bottom

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of reappear

explanation.surface: Crowds return, captivated by skimpy swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large, dense mass of people, a synonym of crowd as a noun.

clue.text: First couple in parade endangered animal

indicators.note: first couple means the opening two letters of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of the word parade
a couple is two things joined, and the joining word is written out
the second letter of the word parade

explanation.surface: The leading pair in a procession are rare animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The first couple of letters in parade are P and A, and writing that out in full, P-AND-A, spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a famous emblem of threatened species, long listed as at risk of extinction.

clue.text: Overly formal to enquire about manned orbiter

indicators.note: about means around, so the nosy word surrounds the spacecraft

parts.note: to pry is to enquire nosily
the International Space Station, abbreviated ISS

explanation.surface: Stuffily asking questions about a crewed spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Prissy describes someone fussily proper and prim, which is being too formal.

clue.text: Statistical processing less responsive on specific form of consumption

parts.note: read as numb-er, more numb, so feeling less
crunching is a particular way of eating

explanation.surface: Data analysis showing less response to a certain type of spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' must be read as the comparative of numb, not the counting word, and 'consumption' means eating, not economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Number crunching is the informal term for heavy calculation and statistical analysis of data.

clue.text: Anyone working to bring about an opening for chaos and irritation

indicators.note: to bring something about is read literally as carrying it around, so it surrounds the rest
working suggests letters set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an opening is a start, so only the first letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: taken as written
the opening letter of chaos

explanation.surface: Anyone at work can cause disorder and aggravation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring about' means put around: the rearranged letters wrap around AN plus the first letter of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance and irritation are both nouns for the feeling of being mildly angered.

clue.text: Shattered about me backing black mark

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for exhausted is read in reverse
about means around, so the reversed word surrounds me

parts.note: shattered is British slang for exhausted
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted admits to a stain on their record.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for exhausted is turned around to DERIT, and ME is placed inside it: DE-ME-RIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a point counted against someone, the same thing as a black mark on a record.

clue.text: Train worker managed to keep line in design

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so managed holds the rest

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: line goes in, placed inside the word for design

parts.note: a design is an intention or aim
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A railway employee succeeded in keeping the track in the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two containers nested: line sits inside design, and that result sits inside managed.
explanation.definitionFit: A railman is someone employed on the railways, so a worker on the trains.

clue.text: Blow up in middle of Hertfordshire, in brief

indicators.note: up is placed in, so it sits inside the county letters
the middle of a word is its centre, so the outer letters are discarded

parts.note: the county is abbreviated HERTS, and its middle three letters are kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something explodes in the heart of a county north of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' wants to be read as one phrase; only 'Blow' defines, and 'up' is placed inside. Hertfordshire is an English county just north of London, written HERTS for short.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that blows is one that bursts out violently, which is what erupting means.

clue.text: Large yard surrounding a place of God

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so the word for large goes around a

parts.note: monster as an adjective means huge
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A big courtyard encloses a holy site.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside the word for huge, and the yard abbreviation is added at the end; 'Large yard' reads as a pair but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is a religious house where monks live in devotion, so a building given over to worship.

clue.text: Mild distinction about island plague

indicators.note: about means around, so the subtle difference wraps around the island

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle difference
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A subtle difference surrounding an island disease outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague, in the weakened sense of a pest or bother, is a nuisance; both are nouns here.

clue.text: Marijuana underlying dodgy things in entertainment venue

indicators.note: in a down clue, underlying means placed underneath, so the drug comes after
dodgy means unreliable or shady, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: taken as written
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Drugs beneath shady goings-on at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'underlying' puts the drug below the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub or bar open late, a place to go out for entertainment.

clue.text: View singular quantity of film

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a can is the round tin a reel of film is stored in, and so an amount of film

explanation.surface: Watching a single reel of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to look over or survey something, a synonym of the verb to view.

clue.text: Black deed — river's picked up germs

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an act is a deed

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the river is written bottom to top

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A wicked act, and the river has caught some infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black deed' looks like one phrase for an evil act but splits. 'Picked up' lifts the river upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes, some causing disease, which is what germs means colloquially.

clue.text: With assistance, I surpass obstacle

parts.note: a hand is help or assistance, as in lend a hand
taken as written
to cap is to outdo or top

explanation.surface: Someone who gets past a barrier with a bit of help.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a disadvantage or hindrance, so something that stands in the way.

clue.text: Artist who's backed 75 per cent of Eastern philosophical system

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so those letters are read in reverse
three quarters of a four-letter word is three letters, so only part of it is used

parts.note: yoga is a Hindu discipline of body and mind

explanation.surface: A painter who supported most of an Asian school of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Only three quarters of the four-letter system is turned round: YOG becomes GOY while the final A stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter and printmaker, so an example of an artist.

clue.text: Guy restraining a dog without a tail — this dog?

indicators.note: a word without its tail loses its final letter
restraining means holding back, so the guy holds the rest within

parts.note: a guy is a man, a male
a plus mutt, a mongrel, which then loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A man holding back a dog with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'this dog?' makes the whole clue point at the answer: a breed, built from a man holding a tailless dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alaskan malamute is a large sled-dog breed, so it is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Vermin run up round top of oven, making you draw back

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means written from the bottom, so everything is reversed
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
round means surrounding, so the vermin go around the next piece

parts.note: lice are parasitic pests
the top letter of oven
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Pests scurrying around the oven make you flinch.
explanation.walkthrough: The vermin wrap round the oven's first letter, run is added, and the lot reads upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring back or flinch away, which is to draw back.

clue.text: Writer's last to be moved by acidic reviewer

indicators.note: the final letter of writer is shifted to a new place, rearranging the word

parts.note: citric acid gives fruit its sourness

explanation.surface: An author's latest work gets a sour review.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of writer is the R; moving it within the word for acidic rearranges it into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic is someone who reviews books, plays or films professionally.

clue.text: Drink round south Mediterranean island mostly confidential

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the island loses its last letter
round means surrounding, so the drink goes around south

parts.note: to tope is an old verb for drinking heavily
S is the abbreviation for south
Crete, the Greek island, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A boozy holiday on a Greek island that is kept very hush-hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Top secret is the highest classification of confidential material, so extremely confidential.

clue.text: Staff taken aback about City ornamentation

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed stick surrounds the City
taken aback is read literally as taken backwards, so the stick is reversed

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
EC is the postcode district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Employees are startled by the decorations in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees but is a stick. The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the decoration and furnishing style of a room, so its ornamentation.

clue.text: King Harry maybe appearing heartless — something you can find in Shakespeare

definitions.text: something you can find in Shakespeare

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: a word without its heart loses its middle, keeping only the outside letters

parts.note: only the outside letters of Harry remain
only the outside letters of maybe remain

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Henry V, perhaps, appearing without courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Harry' suggests Shakespeare's Henry V; instead the king is R, and both Harry and maybe lose their insides.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's verse often uses rhyme, such as rhyming couplets that close scenes.

clue.text: Allege shortfall in uncontaminated wine

indicators.note: a shortfall is a deficit, so the word comes up one letter short

parts.note: pure, falling one letter short
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Claiming there is a deficit of unadulterated wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To purport is to claim or profess, often falsely, which matches allege as a verb.

clue.text: Fear city rioting doing for area? Right

indicators.note: rioting suggests disorder, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
doing for is slang for killing off, so the area letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A frightened town in turmoil wonders whether to wipe out a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing for' means killing off, so the area letter is struck out before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to correct it, and rectify is a verb for making something correct.

clue.text: Drink a lot of beer — get completely smashed?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the beer loses its last letter

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
ale, with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A drinking binge ending in getting thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' suggests drunkenness, but the definition means wrecking a car: to total a vehicle is to write it off.
explanation.definitionFit: In car slang, to total a vehicle is to damage it beyond repair, so it is wrecked utterly.

clue.text: Winner with time to quaff new celebratory drink

parts.note: a champ is a champion, a winner

indicators.note: to quaff is to swallow, so the outer words take the letter inside

parts.note: an age is a period of time
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The victor takes a moment to down some fresh bubbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling wine traditionally opened to toast a victory or special occasion.
